subject: [PATCH v3 5/7] sched/numa: scan PID-inactive VMAs for promotion

2026-09-22.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) memory tiering logic to scan PID-inactive VMAs (Virtual Memory Areas) for promotion, bypassing a filter that previously suppressed faults needed to promote hot slow-tier memory. The patch introduces a new field in the vma_numab_state structure to track the last completed placement scan separately from other scans. This change allows inactive VMAs to receive promotion-only scans without advancing the placement-starvation horizon. As a result, the patch improves memory tiering and reduces CXL bandwidth utilization on a host with 768 GB of DRAM and 256 GB of CXL memory.
